items.question: What attainment becomes dear to the yoginis through this practice?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are named together
A great accomplishment is specified
This accomplishment becomes dear to the yoginis
items.inference: The practice yields a great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginis through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes upon emergence in the moon island?
premises: Emergence in the moon island is indicated
A chapter is identified by ordinal number
The ninth chapter is named
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes with emergence in the moon island.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, having emerged in the moon island.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self standing amid surrounding fire?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire
The self stands on one foot
A specific posture is described
items.inference: The practitioner should envision the self encircled by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The speaker addresses the god
The determination of knowledge is sought
The request asks for it to be made manifest now
items.inference: The speaker asks the god to reveal the determination of knowledge today.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of eight groups of eight is sought to be fully known?
premises: A division into eight groups of eight is named
Full knowledge of this division is desired
The desire is expressed as endless or complete
items.inference: The speaker seeks to fully know the division of the eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: I wish to fully know the division of the eight groups of eight in its entirety.

items.question: How does accomplishment arise quickly in the secret place and wheel, O Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is mentioned
A wheel is mentioned as the locus
Accomplishment occurs quickly there
items.inference: In the secret place, as in the wheel, accomplishment is attained quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how accomplishment comes quickly in the secret place and in the wheel.

items.question: Why is the question asked by the great goddess considered difficult even for gods?
premises: The goddess is praised for her question
The speaker acknowledges being asked
The matter asked about is hard for gods to obtain
items.inference: The goddess has asked about a matter that is well posed but difficult even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess; you have asked me about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead
Specific syllables are mapped to bodily sites
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region
The syllable śa is placed in the heart
The mapping continues the prior assignment
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared to the beloved?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared
Their meditation is now to be taught
The beloved is asked to listen
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have now been declared; O beloved, hear their meditation.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first group of eight described?
premises: A divine lotus is described
The lotus has eight spokes
It is adorned by the first group of eight
items.inference: The first meditation involves a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.

items.question: What conduct should the practitioner abandon after gaining mental equanimity through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal or balanced mind
Village customs are named as something to abandon
An injunction to abandon them is given
items.inference: Through practice and mental equanimity, the practitioner should abandon ordinary village customs.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to social or conventional duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with a balanced mind, one should abandon the customs of village life.

items.question: What powers of distant hearing and bond-paralysis arise from this practice?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is named
Paralysis of bonds is named
These are presented as attained results
items.inference: The practice yields the power to hear from afar and to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean arresting or stunning bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments of immortality and transformation are briefly stated?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment
Transformation is named as an attainment
The teaching is given in brief
items.inference: In brief, the practice also brings immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may mean change of form or reversal
items.plain_english: O goddess, in brief, one also attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled locus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second locus is introduced
It is eight-petaled
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire
items.inference: The second eight-petaled locus is vividly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability to assume many forms arises from a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes one-pointed in meditation
Many forms are produced
This is presented as a resulting power
items.inference: With a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation, one can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: With a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation, one can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power over the moving and unmoving triple world arises in anger?
premises: The practitioner becomes angry
The entire triple world is the object
Both moving and unmoving beings are included
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner can destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced
It is described as a liberator
Its scope is the nine principles
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates one from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava-tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles
items.plain_english: The third is the great wheel, which liberates one from the nine principles.

items.question: What powers over aging and distant seeing result from this wheel?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named
Seeing from very far away is named
Both are presented as attained powers
items.inference: This wheel grants the removal of wrinkles and grey hair and the ability to see from very far away.
items.plain_english: One gains the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: What solitary practice enables one to assume many forms through focused meditation?
premises: The practice is done in solitude
Many forms are to be made
The practitioner must be intent on meditation
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should practice assuming many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make many forms.

items.question: How does constant dedicated practice lead to the attainment of immortality?
premises: Immortality is attained
The practitioner is intent on constant practice
The result follows from sustained effort
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What effect does abstaining from food by day have on death by aging?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified
Death associated with age is named
The practitioner will go beyond it
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death by aging.
uncertainties: nāśanena may mean fasting or destruction; context suggests fasting
items.plain_english: By fasting during the day, one will overcome death due to aging.

items.question: What youthful bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant practice through yoga is performed
A duration of sixteen years is indicated
The body takes on a corresponding form
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi-aṣṭa-varṣa-ākṛtiḥ is taken as the form of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power to shake the triple world arises from contemplating a smoky color?
premises: A smoky color is contemplated always
The triple world is the object affected
The practitioner gains the power to shake it
items.inference: By constantly contemplating a smoky color, one can shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoky color, one can shake the triple world.
